title: The Price of an Explanation: What Demanding Verifiable Artifacts Costs, and What It Buys Back
abstract: arXiv:2611.25896v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Generative models produce many candidate solutions but provide no intrinsic signal by which to rank them. One mitigation is to demand a \emph{verifiable artifact}: a program that can be executed against the available evidence. A common concern is that requiring executable verification incurs costs in both solution quality and computational budget. We measure these two costs on the $120$-task ARC-AGI-2 evaluation set. Demanding a verifiable artifact from an LLM reduced the score from $93$ to $68$ of $120$ tasks ($77\%$ to $57\%$). Of those $25$ tasks, $21$ were reached by no program-producing configuration we ran, at any budget, by sampling or by search; yet for $27$ of the $28$ tasks that only the answer-only arm solved, some program arm held a program that reproduced every demonstration and still failed the test. translated_title: 解释的代价：要求可验证产物损失了什么，又换回了什么
translated_abstract: 生成模型会产生许多候选解，却没有任何内在信号可用于对它们排序。一种缓解手段是要求提供“可验证产物”：即一个可对照现有证据执行的程序。人们普遍担心，要求可执行验证会在解答质量和计算预算两方面带来成本。我们在包含120个任务的ARC-AGI-2评测集上测量了这两类成本。要求LLM提供可验证产物后，其得分从120个任务中的93个降至68个（77%降至57%）。在损失的这25个任务中，有21个任务在我们运行过的任何程序生成配置下——无论何种预算、无论采样还是搜索——都未能解决；然而，在仅由“只给答案”组解决的28个任务中，有27个任务上某些程序组所持有的程序能够复现全部演示示例，却仍在测试上失败。瓶颈在于获得能够“泛化”的解释，而非“找到”某个解释。对两个……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文在ARC-AGI-2上量化了要求LLM生成可执行可验证产物（程序）的代价（得分从77%降至57%），并指出真正的瓶颈在于让解释“泛化”而非“找到”解释——因为多数仅由只答组解出的任务中，程序组其实已拥有能复现全部演示、却仍在测试上失败的程序。
en_tdlr: On ARC-AGI-2, demanding verifiable executable programs from LLMs costs 25 of 120 tasks (77%→57%), but the real bottleneck is generalization rather than finding an explanation, since program arms often already held programs that reproduced all demonstrations yet still failed the test.
